correctness.rationale: Fourier inversion is valid when q and n are coprime. The bilinear quandle multiplication yields precisely y_r=y_{2r}y_{-r}. Each nonzero H_t orbit has root-of-unity order N_t; q-Frobenius cycles impose z^{q^{e_t}}=z^{rho_t(q^{e_t})}. Their common roots number gcd(N_t,q^{e_t}-a_t), and a modular group-order argument proves their existence in the proper splitting field. Independent basis-product enumeration verifies 15 concrete cases, including GF4 and composite n, without substituting for the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Relative to inspected quandle-ring papers, the claim is the all-odd-order finite-field arithmetic product and parameterization. Elhamdadi–Ta–Virgin arXiv:2609.03799 establishes the same Fourier product identity over complex coefficients; this is fully acknowledged. Earlier 2020 and 2022 sources give selected integral or binary idempotents. Comparison by implication found no inspected complete finite-field Galois-coset enumeration; remaining priority risk is real, especially alternative cyclotomic formulations.
residual_risks: An equivalent complete arithmetic product may be recorded under Takasaki core, Alexander quandle, cyclic quasigroup algebra or cyclotomic-coordinate terminology.
The September 2026 Fourier theorem provides the main identity, substantially reducing method novelty; finite-field enumeration is the distinct claim.
arXiv:2608.01550 and arXiv:2206.10386 were not inspected throughout; their abstracts/excerpts cannot certify noncoverage.
Characteristic dividing n is not covered.

value.rationale: Idempotent counts are a standard intrinsic algebra invariant used in quandle-ring constructions and link coloring. This formula determines the entire invariant for all odd n and coprime prime powers q, including composite n, with explicit parameterization and proven arithmetic sensitivity for fixed R_11 over distinct fields. It addresses a natural structural enumeration rather than an arbitrary slice or recomputation of small cases.
